top_story: The most immediate regional shift is Iran’s offer on 22 September to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if Washington reduces military pressure and ends its blockade on Iranian ports, signaling a calibrated attempt to trade de-escalation for economic relief rather than sustain open confrontation. A day earlier in Jerusalem, Netanyahu’s appearance in tunnels beneath Al-Aqsa and Ben Gvir’s heavily protected incursion into the compound sharpened a long-running contest over holy sites that repeatedly feeds wider Palestinian anger and regional mobilization. In Gaza, that political and military escalation continues to register most brutally at the civilian level, where a pregnant woman living in a tent after an airstrike killed her three children and a 12-year-old boy fearing bombardment at work embody how war has collapsed any boundary between survival and ordinary life. The regional picture is one of leaders testing leverage through symbolic provocation and strategic choke points while civilians, especially in Gaza, absorb the deepest and most enduring cost.
